newsitem.title: USA: California firm to repay Russia for missing jewels.
newsitem.headline: California firm to repay Russia for missing jewels.

text.p: A California diamond-cutting firm under investigation for allegedly stealing Russian gold and jewels has agreed to pay the Russian government more than $165 million, the San Francisco Chronicle reported on Saturday.
The Golden ADA court settlement was approved in San Francisco on Thursday by a U.S. District Court judge, the newspaper reported.

The settlement stemmed from a lawsuit filed in September to recover gold, diamonds and other valuables sent from Russia to Golden ADA in 1993 and 1994 as collateral for a loan, according to Martin Beck, an attorney who represented the Committee of the Russian Federation on Precious Metals and Gems.

The committee had accused the former owners of Golden ADA of "misappropriating the Russian assets and using them to purchase a jet aircraft, luxury autos, real estate across northern California, and otherwise squandering the valuables," the Chronicle reported.

Rajiv Gosain, the firm's current chief executive officer, told the Chronicle that Golden ADA's assets were between $50 million and $60 million. He said it was not clear where the remaining funds would come from to pay the Russians.
The Golden ADA case has sparked probes by the FBI and the U.S. Internal Revenue Service, the Chronicle reported.
Beck and Gosain were not immediately available to comment on the Chronicle report.
